findings.claim: load_consent() reads whatever is at <loop>/panel-consent.json with no check that the file is actually untracked/per-checkout; nothing stops that file from being force-added to git (git add -f) despite the .gitignore convention, so a maliciously committed panel-consent.json would still authorize remote egress or cmd-shell execution on every clone/checkout.
findings.note: REJECTED as fixed. The no-.git half IS genuinely closed — verified end to end in a bare scratch dir: the run prints the refusal and the cmd lane is skipped, no pwned file (and PANEL_REVIEW_CONSENT_NO_GIT is NOT documented in SKILL.md, so it cannot leak into the agent workflow by copy-paste; the selftest only sets it in its own process env). But the SAME bundled-archive attack still succeeds whenever the export is unpacked ANYWHERE under an unrelated checkout, which is the common case ($HOME as a dotfiles repo, a monorepo, any workspace repo): git answers rc=1 'untracked' for the attacker's file, load_consent takes it as consent, and no opt-in is required. CONFIRMED live: scratch git init at victimrepo/, then victimrepo/downloaded-bundle/.review-loop/{panel.json with a cmd lane, panel-consent.json approving that exact string, briefs/round-0.*} — `panel_review.py run .review-loop 0` with the env var UNSET executed the shell and wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/pwned-r3.txt. So the stderr text and CONTROLS.md's 'Outside a git checkout the script fails CLOSED (a ZIP/`git archive` export keeps a force-added consent file)' overstate the guarantee: the export only fails closed if it is extracted outside every checkout. Root cause: git-tracked-ness of a file that SHIPS WITH THE PAYLOAD is not a trust boundary — 'untracked' proves only 'not committed to whatever repo happens to be above', never 'created by this human on this machine'. The only closure is machine-local state the bundle cannot carry: keep consent OUT of the loop dir, e.g. ~/.config/panel-review/consent-<sha256 of the abs loop path>.json (or an HMAC in the in-loop file keyed by a home-dir secret). Until then the in-tree fail-closed cases are honest and the docs must not claim more than they deliver. | Round 4: FIXED - verified INDEPENDENTLY, not from the selftest. Replayed the bundled-archive repro in scratch against HEAD with the REAL ~/.config (no XDG override): (a) bundle unpacked UNDER an unrelated git checkout (git reports it '?? downloaded-bundle/', i.e. untracked - the exact round-3 fail-open) -> lane 'evil' status=skipped, marker file never created, rc=0; (b) no-.git bundle with a cmd lane AND a codex lane -> both skipped, no marker. The stderr hint names the CORRECT machine-local path: I recomputed sha256(realpath('.review-loop')) by hand and it matches the printed 00be8454...a0f4.json. consent_path is stable across absolute / trailing-slash / relative spellings (three spellings -> one identical path, checked by hand). Positive control: writing the printed file under an XDG override arms exactly the approved cmd string and still refuses the bundle's string (cmd/digest binding intact). No fail-OPEN path found: base comes from env/HOME and the key from realpath, neither of which the reviewed repo can influence; a missing, unreadable, directory-at-path, malformed, or non-object consent file all return {}. Mutants re-run by me: killed 6 survived 0 errors 0 mismatches 0, including legacy-inrepo-consent-honored and consent-path-keyed-by-basename. consent_git_status / in_git_worktree / PANEL_REVIEW_CONSENT_NO_GIT are gone from code, selftest and all four docs (grepped repo-wide: zero remnants). merge_ledger.py:444-450 KEEP change is coherent - KEEP means 'leave in the loop dir', so the legacy file stays put and keeps firing its hint instead of being swept to legacy/; nothing else special-cases it.

findings.claim: consent_path()'s key is sha256(os.path.realpath(loop)) with no case folding, so on case-insensitive-but-case-preserving filesystems (default macOS APFS, NTFS) the same loop directory spelled with different casing hashes to two different consent files, producing spurious 'no consent, lanes skipped' and duplicate consent files.
findings.note: Panel final-pass finding, minted at closeout; implementer declined and the argument HOLDS. Case-folding the key would make consent recorded for /repo/A also authorize /repo/a, which on a case-SENSITIVE filesystem (ext4, case-sensitive APFS volumes) are genuinely different loop dirs -- i.e. the cheap fix trades a fail-closed nuisance for a fail-open grant of remote-egress/shell consent. Today's failure mode is a consent miss with lanes skipped and a stderr line naming the consent-path verb, which is recoverable in one command. Any real fix must be filesystem-capability-aware (probe case-insensitivity of the loop dir's volume), which is not worth the surface. Routes to BACKLOG as documentation, not as work.

findings.claim: run_cmd's timeout path calls os.killpg, which does not exist on Windows, and AttributeError is not in the contextlib.suppress allowlist -- a cmd-lane timeout on Windows raises instead of killing the process group, so the lane reports status=error (caught by run_lane's broad except) and the shell's children are left running.
findings.note: Panel final-pass finding (verifier demoted major->minor: blast radius is one lane, not the script), minted at closeout, NOT actioned by the closeout. Routes to BACKLOG -- fix is one line (guard on hasattr(os,'killpg') else p.kill()) if Windows support is ever claimed.
